description: On / off toggle. Radix renders a <button role="switch"> with aria-checked reflecting the current state. The visual thumb slides via data-checked:translate-x. Three sizes: sm (32 x 18.4px, 16px thumb), default (44 x 24px, 20px thumb inset 2px) and lg (52 x 28px, 24px thumb inset 2px). Unlike Checkbox, there is no indeterminate state.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to / from the switch.

focus.notes: Uses focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50 with focus-visible:border-ring, and an invisible ::after hit area extending 8px sideways and vertically to at least 44px tall on every size (sm 46.4 x 48px, default 44 x 60px, lg 44 x 68px). Disabled switches show cursor-not-allowed and opacity-50 but remain in the tab order unless tabIndex={-1} is added.

announcements: Announces as "switch" with its accessible name and current on / off state.
screenReader.notes: Switch has no visible label of its own. Always pair with a <Label htmlFor> or wrap in a <label>, or provide aria-label / aria-labelledby. For settings with an immediate effect, Switch is usually the right choice over Checkbox because users perceive it as a live toggle.

contrast.ui: Checked track is the brand orange with a 1px border-primary-ink edge (4.9:1 on the cream background, 5.0:1 on cards); unchecked track is bg-input (3.9:1). The orange fill itself is about 2.3:1, so the ink edge carries the non-text contrast. In dark mode primary-ink is the orange, at about 8:1 on espresso

motion.reducedMotion: Thumb uses transition-transform. Gate with motion-reduce:transition-none if you need strict reduced-motion compliance; the state is still conveyed by position + color.

consumerResponsibilities: Provide an accessible name via a linked <Label> or aria-label; the switch alone has none.
Use Switch for settings that take effect immediately (autoSave, notifications). Use Checkbox for form fields that require a Submit.
Don't rely on color alone to convey state; Radix already uses position (thumb left / right) as a secondary indicator, which works for color-blind users.
